design: MemorySearchService.search implements searchMemory on the closed MemorySearchRequest of reports/contracts/ocor-governed-memory.openapi.yaml: exact envelope + search field set, GCS rebuilt from the authenticated binding with digest recalculation, deadline, registered named/versioned query contract bound to one mode, closed per-mode parameters (text; vector + vector_profile pin; optional closed filters), kinds/scopes against the capability matrix (UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY), top_k <= 100, registered ranking profile, valid_at not beyond the boundary clock. Every malformed request is refused before policy, stop state, audit or any index read.

Policy before lookup: the live MemoryRetrievalPolicy.authorize_retrieval decision must be permitted, evaluated on the context policy bundle (STALE_POLICY) and cover every requested kind/scope (AUTHORITY_DENIED). The authorized partition set is derived from the partition tuple alone: same tenant and organization (cross-tenant deny-by-default), same domain or explicit cross-domain Authority, compartments within the caller's, requested scope, same or compatible purpose, accepted policy bundle and ontology release, every scope-owner binding (run, task, agent, team, project, federation policy) explicitly granted, caller marking dominating the partition marking. Index searches run only inside those partitions; denials are audited.

Policy before materialisation: every candidate is re-read from the metadata authority and must be COMMITTED, the item's head version (superseded/corrected/reclassified versions never match), ACTIVE without deletion epoch, of a requested kind/scope in the capability matrix, valid at valid_at, unexpired on the boundary clock, inside the caller's compartments and marking, accepted by the pinned filters, and permitted by authorize_materialization. Ineligible hits are dropped before they occupy a candidate slot; the page widens until the pool holds the best eligible candidates (fail-closed RETRIEVAL_BACKPRESSURE beyond max_candidates).

Ranking (RankingProfile, versioned and digested): lexical score normalised over the eligible pool only, vector cosine of the pinned representation version, recency half-life on the boundary clock, confidence, source quality per source kind, policy (taint) multiplier and greedy same-source diversity are recorded separately in score_factors; final_score = (sum of weighted relevance/prior factors) x policy x diversity. Scores are retrieval evidence, not truth.

Materialisation re-checks the stop epoch (kill switch / delegation revocation -> STOP_EPOCH_MISMATCH, no hit) and re-validates each ranked version (CANDIDATE_CHANGED if it changed), then reads it through MemoryStoreCoordinator.read_version (committed, projections bound, content decrypted and digest-checked). The audit receipt pins the query (contract digest, mode, kinds, scopes, text, query-vector digest, vector representation version, filters, valid_at, top_k, ranking profile digest, explanation flag), the representation versions searched, the authorization and authorized-partition digest, the stop epoch, the evaluation time and every hit's exact version ref, item digest, content digest and score; audit_ref is its digest and is recorded through the audit port before the answer (no audit, no answer).

No result or candidate cache exists: every request recomputes candidates from the metadata authority and the partitioned projections, so the cache channel cannot carry influence (ADD v1.3 Part II §2.8). Metrics use a bounded label set (mode or UNPARSED x OK or a Problem reason code).

inputs_tree_definition: git rev-parse <commit>:inputs (tree della directory inputs/ immutabile)
normative_interpretations: Only ACTIVE versions are retrievable; PROPOSED and QUARANTINED are not yet admitted to use, and SUPERSEDED/REVOKED/EXPIRED/LEGAL_HOLD/DELETION_* are absent from result, rank, count and explanation (LLD §7.2 FGM-10). A version is current only if it is the item's committed head: a later version in a partition the caller cannot read hides the earlier one instead of revealing it (reclassification is absence, not existence).

Cross-project, cross-domain and federated retrieval require explicit Authority in the pre-query decision (granted project ids, domains, federation policy refs); cross-tenant and cross-organization retrieval is denied without exception because no separately approved federation-access policy profile exists in this baseline.

Result marking per hit is the conservative join computed through the marking lattice over the returned item's marking, which admission (0050) already bounds above every input and lineage source; no response-level marking exists in the closed MemorySearchResponse.

MemoryHit and MemorySearchResponse serialise to the exact closed OpenAPI field sets; explanations are policy-safe records built only from authorized, eligible data and referenced by explanation_ref (content-addressed); raw vectors are never returned.

STRUCTURED retrieval reads the metadata authority (no index) and ranks by the profile's prior factors; FULL_TEXT and VECTOR rank by their own representation plus priors; HYBRID unions the two eligible pools.

Lifecycle versions after admission (REVOKED) are produced in the tests through the ledger port and the real coordinator, as the lifecycle coordinator (OCOR-DEV-0055) will; retrieval only consumes them.
raw_output_format: JSONL: una riga per comando/artefatto/osservazione con label, command, exit_code, sha256 dei byte UTF-8 archiviati e output integrale; le credenziali locali generate (valori di .ocor/bootstrap.env) sono sostituite da <redacted:NAME> prima dell'archiviazione e dell'hash, gli originali restano solo fuori da Git; DSN mostrato come <local generated credential>

requirement_results.command: on real PostgreSQL (metadata, encrypted content, full-text), Qdrant (vector) and OpenBao transit: STRUCTURED reads the metadata authority with pinned filters (source kind, content schema, confidence, taint), FULL_TEXT and VECTOR rank by their own representation, HYBRID records lexical, vector, recency, confidence, source-quality, diversity and policy factors separately with final_score recomputable from the versioned profile; a parallel embedding representation is searched only under its own pin

the audit receipt pins query contract, mode, kinds, scopes, text, query-vector digest, representation versions, filters, valid_at, top_k and ranking profile digest, plus every hit's exact version ref, item and content digest; every pinned dimension changes query_digest; identical state replays byte-identically, also across fresh adapters; a new version is a new exact pin and the earlier version stays readable; hits of another representation version fail closed

malformed requests, missing or foreign bindings and GCS mismatches are refused before policy and any index read; pre-query denial, stale bundle, unauthorized kind/scope and policy outage are audited and read no candidate; cross-project, cross-domain and federated retrieval open only with explicit Authority, cross-tenant stays denied; materialisation policy outage and unbound item digests fail closed

two real-backend worlds, one with 21 unauthorized items of distinct classes (compartment, mixed compartments, tenant, organization, marking, purpose, domain, project, run, agent, federated, quarantined, proposed, expired, not yet valid, validity elapsed, pending, revoked, materialisation-denied, other kind, reclassified): byte-identical responses, explanations and receipts in all four modes; indexes searched only inside authorized partitions; a query matching only unauthorized items is indistinguishable from no match; ineligible hits never displace eligible candidates

revoked, expired (boundary clock) and reclassified items disappear from result, rank, count, normalisation and explanation; a SECRET caller sees only the reclassified head; a kill switch or delegation revocation between planning and materialisation fails closed with no hit and no success receipt
a version left PENDING by a Qdrant outage is never returned; a committed full-text projection tampered in PostgreSQL blocks materialisation with REPRESENTATION_NOT_READY and no success receipt

residual_risks: Real PostgreSQL/Qdrant/OpenBao adapters are reused from the 0051 task test module (CompactQdrantVectorIndex only sets one segment and a 1 MiB WAL per collection because the sealed 0023 harness keeps Qdrant storage on a 256 MiB tmpfs); no production adapter under memory/adapters/ exists yet.

Ineligible versions inside an authorized partition (lifecycle, validity, filters) never change a returned answer, but more than max_candidates of them ahead of the eligible pool turn the answer into a fail-closed RETRIEVAL_BACKPRESSURE (and beyond the 0051 scan bound into UNBOUND_BACKLOG); partitions the caller is not authorized for never influence it. Lifecycle compaction is OCOR-DEV-0055/0056.

Timing buckets are not equalised: the evidence shows that unauthorized partitions are never searched and that responses are byte-identical with and without unauthorized items, not constant-time execution. Listing partitions reads every partition tuple of the metadata store (no content, no index).

Query embeddings are supplied by the caller with their representation pin; embedding generation, model upgrade and rebuild are OCOR-DEV-0053. Lifecycle transitions are OCOR-DEV-0055, deletion saga OCOR-DEV-0056, context assembly and influence receipts OCOR-DEV-0057, quotas OCOR-DEV-0059.

Test-level anonymous Docker volume leaks in pre-existing suites remain allocated to OCOR-DEV-REM-0018 (see the full-suite resource attribution); the 0052 task suite itself leaves no container, volume or network (task-teardown-delta).
